correctness.rationale: Over arbitrary k, the incidence factorization is finite and birational from a smooth product. On c0=1, the normalization B=A[x]/Q is free of rank n over A=k[b,c1,...,cn]; R is the A-submodule with basis 1,bx,...,b^(n-1)x^(n-1). The generic irreducibility of Q over k(c1,...,cn) makes multiplication by a nonzero residue invertible, ruling out conductor elements of b-adic order less than n−1. Therefore c=(a,b)^(n−1), globally by coordinate changes/descent. Coefficient derivatives give the entire Jacobian; when p divides n the Euler-derived factor G yields two independent degree n−1 jets and the stated length. The polar-degree and arithmetic formulas follow. Standalone symbolic and finite-projective enumeration checks replayed successfully; their finite scope is explicit.

value.rationale: The family S(1,n) is a natural classical scroll, and its projective dual is a fundamental discriminantal hypersurface. The exact global conductor measures nonnormality in all degrees, and the abrupt polar-degree collapse precisely when the characteristic divides n links this nonnormality to wild differential behavior. The generic transverse Jacobian length and uniform arithmetic formula give concrete geometric consequences. These are global structural invariants of an infinite natural family, not arbitrary tiny examples or only a recovered known polynomial.
